checked_sources.result: Primary reference for non-partitioned PFA/ARL e-detectors, start-weight semantics, and Gaussian information-rate context.

checked_sources.result: Primary source for Gaussian/exponential-family SNML logarithmic regret used by the existing r68-r69 certificate.

checked_sources.source: Zhang, Xu & Chen 2012, The Exact Likelihood Ratio Test for Equality of Two Normal Populations
checked_sources.result: Confirms an exact finite-sample null distribution for the two-normal homogeneity LRT; useful for tightening test calibration but not by itself an exact alternative-side power certificate.

checked_sources.source: Takemoto & Arizono 2002, The Power of Likelihood Ratio Tests for Homogeneity of Two Normal Populations
checked_sources.result: Derives finite-sample cumulants of the log-LR under arbitrary normal alternatives and an approximation to its alternative distribution/power, with simulation comparison. This is a candidate tightening route, not an exact lower-tail guarantee.

derived_results.claim: For the exact-split Gaussian two-segment population log-likelihood gain at fixed D_KL(Q||P)=I with P=N(0,1), the hardest direction on the entire KL level set is the pure variance-increase endpoint, not a mixed mean/variance change.
derived_results.statement: Parameterize Q=N(mu,r) by mu^2(r)=2I+log r-r+1 on the feasible interval r in [r_-(I),r_+(I)], where endpoints solve 0.5[-log r+r-1]=I. Let lambda=m/(m+n), q=1-lambda and V=lambda+q r+lambda q mu^2. The population two-segment-vs-pooled Gaussian gain is G_pop=(m+n)/2[log V-q log r]. Along the KL level, V'=q[q+lambda/r], so d/dr[2G_pop/(m+n)] = q[(q r+lambda)-V]/(rV) = -lambda*q^2*mu^2/(rV) <= 0, strictly below zero whenever mu^2>0. Hence G_pop is minimized at r=r_+(I), mu=0. This closes the population-information geometry over the whole normalized Gaussian KL level set.

derived_results.claim: The existing r69 prospective union/box lower certificate is not geometry-tight: it reports a mixed mean/variance direction as worst even though the exact population information theorem puts the worst direction at pure variance increase.
derived_results.interpretation: The mixed-direction failure comes from separately lower-bounding mean separation and segment variances, then minimizing over a rectangular uncertainty set. It is a failure of the current sufficient certificate, not evidence that mixed changes are intrinsically hardest.

derived_results.claim: Under the current conservative r69 certificate, full KL-level exact-split coverage can be restored without increasing the existing 52 individualized states by delaying deterministic scale activation while keeping the old spacing/lifetime values.
derived_results.comparison: If activation times are held at the old values instead, the same certificate needs H approximately 641, 769 and 1122 respectively; keeping the old spacings would require 41+25+18=84 individualized states. Thus the certificate exposes a concrete capacity-vs-activation-delay tradeoff.

derived_results.claim: The mixed-direction certificate failure was not reflected in a common-random exact-SNML engineering scan; over the sampled KL level, empirical lower-tail evidence was weakest at the variance-increase endpoint and remained far above threshold.
derived_results.details: For each I in {1,0.5,0.25}, 61 log-spaced r values spanning the complete KL level were evaluated with 500 common-random exact-split Gaussian paths at the original T0/H. Every sampled path at every grid point crossed the first-candidate threshold. The lowest 10th-percentile log C occurred at the pure variance-up endpoint: about 48.97 nats for I=1, 54.50 for I=0.5, and 53.79 for I=0.25, versus threshold 5.09 nats. Monte Carlo is engineering evidence only and does not prove a uniform 1-beta guarantee.

derived_results.claim: Burn-in makes split-grid mismatch substantially less damaging than a one-sided d=g calculation suggests: for a change between adjacent candidates, the better of the previous and next candidate retains most population information at the variance-up worst direction.
derived_results.statement: If the previous candidate is early by d<=b=16, all pre-change contamination after that candidate lies inside its unscored local burn-in, so its scored post segment remains pure Q. A late candidate instead contaminates the end of its scored pre segment with Q. For each grid interval, compare the previous candidate early by x and the next candidate late by g-x and take the larger population gain.
derived_results.scope: These retained fractions are population/quasi-likelihood calculations at the pure variance-up endpoint, not finite-sample PFA/power certificates. They show that the correct mismatch object is a two-neighbor max, not a single candidate at worst one-sided offset.

candidates_new.mechanism: Replace independent mean/variance confidence-box degradation with a joint sufficient-statistic/LRT lower-tail certificate that respects the KL-level geometry; use the theorem that the population information worst direction is pure variance increase as a structural target, but do not promote it to a finite-sample worst-direction theorem until proved.
candidates_new.evidence: Exact analytic population derivative plus full-level common-random SNML scan; finite-sample exact-null and alternative-cumulant LRT literature supplies possible tightening machinery.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the population theorem, medium for the proposed finite-sample tightening route.

candidates_new.mechanism: Keep the existing 52-state {H,g} bank but raise deterministic activation prefixes to approximately {321,675,1549} for information floors {1,0.5,0.25} under the current conservative exact-split certificate; separately prove neighbor-grid mismatch before adoption.
candidates_new.evidence: Direct numerical solution of the r69 prospective lower bound over the full normalized KL level.
candidates_new.confidence: high for exact-split certificate arithmetic; not yet sufficient for misaligned changepoints.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Mean-only and variance-only representative alternatives are enough to certify the full Gaussian KL level.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected for the current r69 finite-sample certificate. Its actual minimum lies at mixed mean/variance points with negative margins for all three old scales.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The mixed directions found by r69 are the intrinsically least detectable Gaussian changes at fixed KL.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected at population-information level. An exact derivative proves the population Gaussian GLR decreases monotonically with variance ratio along the KL level and is minimized at pure variance increase.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Use the exact null LRT distribution alone to claim a sharper finite-sample power guarantee.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not valid. Exact null calibration does not give an exact alternative lower tail. Takemoto-Arizono provides finite-sample alternative cumulants/power approximation, but a rigorous 1-beta lower certificate still needs additional work.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Worst split mismatch is obtained by taking one candidate d=g away from the true change.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Too pessimistic for a regular candidate grid. A change is bracketed by previous/next candidates; burn-in can completely absorb early mismatch up to b, so the relevant power object is the maximum evidence of the two neighbors.

frontier: Derive a joint finite-sample lower-tail bound for the two-normal GLR/SNML sufficient statistics that avoids the independent d_minus-plus-variance-box union bound. Determine whether pure variance increase is also the finite-sample worst direction over the whole KL level or produce a certified counterexample.

Formalize split-grid mismatch using the two neighboring candidates. For late starts, the pre scored block is a known two-component sequence of independent Gaussians; for early starts beyond burn-in, the post scored block is similarly contaminated. Use generalized/noncentral quadratic-form concentration or an exact sufficient-statistic representation to obtain a 1-beta lower certificate.

Re-solve {T0_j,g_j,H_j,w_j} under total individualized-state budget 52 only after the two-neighbor mismatch certificate is available. Compare delayed activation against increased lifetime instead of optimizing either in isolation.
Use Zhang-Xu-Chen exact null LRT structure and Takemoto-Arizono finite-sample alternative cumulants as tightening leads, but retain explicit distinction between exact validity and approximation.

Quantify the price of the separable candidate-wise infimum detector relative to the shared-null infimum-after-sum objective under common-random Gaussian paths, because a tighter candidate certificate may otherwise optimize the wrong detector.
Extend beyond Gaussian only after a separate robust finite-sample class is specified; no heavy-tail generalization is licensed by r70.
exact_next_action: Write the two-sample Gaussian GLR entirely in the three independent sufficient statistics available under an exact split (two scaled chi-square sample variances and one normal mean difference), then numerically integrate/optimize its lower tail over the full KL level to identify a much tighter prospective 1-beta bound. Next extend that representation to a late candidate whose pre block contains d post-change observations and to an early candidate with max(d-b,0) pre-change observations in the scored post block; certify the max of the two adjacent candidates for every x in [0,g]. Only then re-optimize the three-scale 52-state bank.
